summary: Iteration 125 — tested the 3 favourites features (account persistence, 'Le tue preferite' row, public ❤N count) on backend + frontend. Backend: 6/6 pytest passed (GET /api/favorites, POST toggle, POST sync, public GET /api/favorites/counts, auth guard, invalid payload, custodite:<id> keys). Frontend (mobile 390x844, admin@mikilab.de): favourited 2 MikiLab recipes from the expanded 'Bread' folder → hearts turned aria-pressed=true, public count badge recipe-fav-count-<id> appeared with value 1 within ~1s; recipe-fav-row appeared above the filters with title 'Your favourites' and mini-cards fav-row-item-<id>; clicking a mini-card opened the detail with fav-recipe-<id> heart already filled (views in sync). F5 reload kept the favourites; logout + clearing localStorage 'mikilab_fav_recipes' + re-login restored both favourites FROM THE SERVER (sync repopulated localStorage) → account persistence confirmed. Row correctly hidden when cat-filter-favs is active and absent when there are 0 favourites (chip shows 'Favourites' with no counter, empty-state message shown). Custodite showcase heart (custodite-fav-matera) toggles and shows count 1 using the custodite:<id> key. All test favourites cleaned up (GET /api/favorites → []).
critical_code_review_comments: lib/favorites.jsx: useFavRecipes mount does sync(local -> server) and takes the server union as truth. Consequence: a guest's localStorage favourites are merged into whichever account logs in on that device, and an un-favourite done on another device can be re-added by this device's stale localStorage. Consider sending only additions made while logged out, or timestamp-based reconciliation (design decision, not blocking).
GET /api/favorites/counts aggregates the whole favorites collection on every call (no index/cache). With growth, add an index on recipe_id or a short server-side cache.
Added missing data-testid custodite-fav-count-<id> in sections/RicetteCustodite.jsx (the count span had none, unlike recipe-fav-count-<id>).
